# Art library

<!-- Generated by `pnpm art library` from apps/activity/src/sprites/concepts/. Do not edit by hand; `pnpm check` fails when it is out of date. -->

Art drawn ahead of its content: creatures, bosses, items and banners that have no name or stats yet. **Before adding content, look here** for art that was made for it, and use it (move the sprite into `apps/activity/src/sprites/data/` under the content id and delete the concept in the same PR). To add art, see `docs/design/art-studio.md`.

Status: **liked** means Misa approved the look; **draft** means he has not said yet; **redo** means he wants changes first (see the notes); **archived** is kept for reference only (a direction not picked, or replaced by newer art).

## Combat v2 icons: attack shapes, board states, store meters

![Combat v2 icons: attack shapes, board states, store meters](combat-icons.png)

- **Status:** draft
- **Requested:** 2026-10-31, Misa: "icons for keywords and attack shapes" (roadmap phase 3, combat v2).
- **Source:** `apps/activity/src/sprites/concepts/combat-icons.ts` (draw it with `pnpm art combat-icons`)
- **Sheet of:** `4312f4866bc3`
- The audit is docs/design/combat/icons.md: which icons are new, which shipped glyphs are used as they are, and which words stay text.
- Misa's review, 2026-11-01. Liked as drawn: Quake, Cross, Checker, One-shot ("really like"), Barrage ("three marks is enough"), Sweep, Crit. Redrawn in round 2 (each replaces the shipped glyph for combat v2, which v1 keeps using): Slam, Strike, Lance, Pincer, Leap, Plain attack, Boost, and the three Store meters.
- Round 2 feedback: Slam "the target, then the adjacent creatures: like the cross, but the centre square bigger, one square left and right". Strike "the right shape, but inside a circle: remove the circle". Lance "should point downwards: the boss attacks from top to bottom". Pincer "a very subtle crab-pincer; the white dot is unnecessary" (both options shown). Leap "like Barrage, but squares, with a faint line between them, a zigzag". Plain attack "should look different from a move: something like a sword". Boost "a star does not look good". Store meters "a box, chest, safe, vault or basket that contains something: one container for all, each holding its own thing; the amount as text beside it (x3), never in the icon".
- Round 2 answers (Misa, 2026-11-01): liked as drawn: Slam, Strike ("different from Cross, good enough"), Lance, Pincer (claws: "looking pretty good"; the plain alternative is removed), the plain attack sword, the three Stores ("nice"). Leap: "it looks like a fork right now; move the bottom square right a pixel or two, so it reads as a chain": done in round 3, awaiting his look. Still draft (not commented on): Boost, Escalating, armour, cracked armour, silence ward, Determination.
- Moved into `glyphs.ts` (2026-11-03, the v2 raid tab used them first): Quake, Cross, Checker, One-shot, Slam, Strike, Lance, Pincer and the plain attack, under the ids they had here. They stand in the sheet as shipped glyphs now. Leap and the six unreviewed ones stay here: a screen draws their drafts (`combat-glyphs.ts`) until Misa answers, then they move too.
- Needs before use: Misa approves the look; each icon gets a glyph id in glyphs.ts, a glossary entry and (shapes) a place in moveLabel; the dungeon modifier "extra crits" then switches from the reticle to the Crit icon.
- Cut order if Misa wants fewer icons: the three Store meter heads (name the resource in text), then the silence ward, then the cracked armour (a crack drawn over the armour icon), then One-shot (it shares the Strike crosshairs).

| Code | Kind | Role | Status | Idea |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape-leap` | glyph | Leap | draft | Leap (was Leaping Strike; redrawn, round 3): the strongest, then the next, softer. Like Barrage but three squares, joined by a faint zigzag line (a bolt, without the bolt that Spark already is). Misa, 2026-11-01: "it looks like a fork right now; move the bottom square right a pixel or two, so it reads as a chain". The bottom square moved 2 pixels right (1 pixel still read as a ">" arrow); the line still joins it. |
| `crit` | glyph | Crit, Sure Crit | liked | A lucky hit that deals double. A gold burst; a Sure Crit counter is this burst with its count ("x2"), never a meter of its own. |
| `armour` | glyph | Armour, Blocked | draft | Armour on the boss card (with its number) and the shield of a Blocked hit (with 0). A steel breastplate, so it is not the Guard's shield. |
| `armour-cracked` | glyph | Will be Blocked | draft | On a creature whose plain hit would be Blocked by the boss's armour: the breastplate with a red crack through it. |
| `escalating` | glyph | Escalating | draft | The boss grows as the weekend goes on, a step at a time. Rising steps, the top one lit. |
| `silence-ward` | glyph | Silence ward | draft | A warded creature cannot be silenced. The Silenced speaker with sound waves instead of a cross. |
| `determination` | glyph | Determination | draft | More damage and healing for each failed weekend on the same boss. A gold arrow rising from a base: more each failed try, up to five. |

## Element shards, told apart by shape

![Element shards, told apart by shape](shards.png)

- **Status:** liked
- **Requested:** 2026-11-03: the element shard icons must differ by shape, not only colour (accessibility review from the valley session; Misa asked to provide what the valley needs).
- **Source:** `apps/activity/src/sprites/concepts/shards.ts` (draw it with `pnpm art shards`)
- **Sheet of:** `effcee065520`
- Misa picked Tide A (rounded), Ember A, Grove A, Spark A, Mire B on 2026-11-03; now in gear-sprites.ts.
- Why: Ember (#ef6a3a) and Grove (#5cbf5a) are a classic deuteranope confusion pair and the shipped shards differ only in the top two rows. The Forge and Market loop is about which shard you need, so each element is a different outline. Colours are unchanged.
- Every sprite has a `deuteranope` alt (Machado 2009, severity 1.0). Its row in the set sheet is the test: five different shapes per variant column.
- Silhouettes: Tide a drop (a) or a curling wave (b); Ember a tall flame with a side tongue (a) or a crown of three flames (b); Grove a leaf on a stem (a) or a two-leaf sprout (b); Spark a bolt (a) or a zigzag (b); Mire a blob with one drip (a) or two drips (b).
- The picks replaced the sprites in `gear-sprites.ts` (BUNDLED_PART_ICONS keeps its ids); scrap and glimmer are untouched. The drafts stay here for reference.

<a id="valley-forge-crate"></a>

## The sealed gear crate

![The sealed gear crate](valley-forge-crate.png)

- **Status:** draft
- **Requested:** 2026-11-14 (via the valley session): collecting gear should be a "big moment": common pieces come home on their own; rare and epic pieces wait in a sealed crate inside the Forge until the player opens it; opening reveals them one by one, best last.
- **Source:** `apps/activity/src/sprites/concepts/valley-forge-crate.ts` (draw it with `pnpm art valley-forge-crate`)
- **Sheet of:** `d84047871d13`
- Crate pieces are `free`, night palette main plus `alts`: `day` (lighter wood, deeper glow so it reads on pale ground), `epic` (pink-violet glow) and `epic-day`. The main palette is the RARE one (blue seam glow); `epic` swaps only the glow keys `g G h s`. Glow colours are the game rarity colours (`--rarity-rare #4da3ff`, `--rarity-epic #ff6fbf`, tints `#7ebcff`, `#f397ff`). Ink, woods and iron are the Forge props (`valley/forge-props.ts`).
- `crate-sealed` 20 x 18: the 14-wide crate body sits at x 3-16 (3 px of margin each side), base row 17. Iron bands, a brass padlock on an iron hasp, a glowing lid gap, a glowing plank joint and glowing vertical joints. CRATE_PROP is 16 x 16; this one is 14 wide and 14 tall inside a 20 x 18 canvas that leaves room for the shake.
- `crate-shake-1`, `-2`, `-3` share the 20 x 18 canvas and base row 17, so they swap in place of the sealed crate: 1 and 2 lean opposite ways (top shifted 1 px) with the lid lifted 1 px (a double glow gap), dust at one foot and two sparks; 3 is upright with dust at both feet. Play sealed, 1, 2, 1, 3 as a rattle. `shake-strip` (80 x 18) shows sealed, 1, 2, 3 side by side.
- `crate-open` 20 x 27: the box takes the bottom 10 rows (y 17-26), its base row 26 sits on the sealed crate base row (row 17): align the bottom rows; the sprite reaches 9 px higher than the sealed canvas. The lid leans against the left wall (x 0-3) and the padlock hangs open; a stepped column of rarity glow rises from the mouth with sparks. Same glow keys, so `epic` and the days work.
- `burst-common`, `burst-rare`, `burst-epic` are 48 x 48 UI overlays, one palette each (no night/day), drawn with a dark rim so they read on dark and on light. The centre 16 x 16 (x 16-31, y 16-31) is empty: draw the revealed item there. Escalation: common is a broken grey ring (radius to 17), rare is a blue ring with eight rays (to 22), epic is a pink-violet ring, sixteen rays to the edge, four-point sparkles and loose sparks.

| Code | Kind | Role | Status | Idea |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `crate-sealed` | free |  | draft | A sturdy iron-banded crate with a brass padlock, light seeping from the lid gap and plank joints. Variations: A (main) the iron-banded crate with a brass padlock, B a treasure chest (domed lid, gold corner caps, a big keyhole plate whose keyhole glows, a glowing seam), C a crate bound with glowing rune-bands and a sigil instead of iron and a lock. Both use the main's keys, so `epic` and `day` recolour them (B and C add no colours). Pick: B, because the chest shape says "treasure" before any glow does, and its keyhole is the one bright spot to tap. |

<a id="valley-forge-interior"></a>

## The Forge, inside

![The Forge, inside](valley-forge-interior.png)

- **Status:** draft
- **Requested:** 2026-11-11 (via the valley session): clicking the Forge goes inside, into a workshop interior. "It would be cool to have the same stuff there (my creatures working at the anvils) but also see some other creatures working in the background, a fire going, etc. Basically make it look like the interior of a workshop."
- **Source:** `apps/activity/src/sprites/concepts/valley-forge-interior.ts` (draw it with `pnpm art valley-forge-interior`)
- **Sheet of:** `7c46281ec723`
- Pieces the game lays out behind its existing props (`valley/forge-props.ts`: anvil, chest, crate, plans table; creatures stand in front at the anvils). Level 3 look: sandstone, timber, black iron, terracotta. Same ink and woods as the props. Night is the main palette (fire is the light, windows dark blue with a moon glint); `alts.day` recolours the same pixels (windows bright, daylight patches `b` on the wall and `B` on the floor).
- `back-wall` 128 x 56 tiles sideways (column 0 continues column 127; a timber post crosses the seam; see `seam` and `seam-day`). Beam on rows 0-5, terracotta frieze 6-8, windows at x 20 and x 84 (opening 13-34, sill 35-39), plinth 48-55. Stand it on the floor line: its bottom row is the base.
- `furnace` 48 x 52: body base on row 51, mouth fire at x 14-33 (mouth centre x 24). Place it so the base row sits a few rows below the wall bottom.
- `furnace-glow` 128 x 40, a floor overlay the game draws over the floor tiles and under the props. It carries the flagstone pattern in lit colours, so its origin (0, 0) must sit on a floor tile corner (x and y multiples of 16 from the floor's own origin). Anchor: the pool centre is at x 25, y 6 in the overlay, which is the furnace mouth centre (furnace x + 23) and the furnace base line (furnace y + 51) when the overlay's top row is the floor's top row. In the preview: furnace (2, 11), overlay (0, 56). Night: four warm tones, brightest at the mouth, reaching right to about x 128 and fading. By day the two outer rings are the plain floor colours, so only a small warm patch (about 40 px wide) shows at the mouth.
- `shelf` 32 x 16 and `tool-rack` 32 x 24 hang on the wall; `hanging-tools` 24 x 16 hangs from the beam (its top row touches the beam bottom, row 5 of the wall).
- `workbench` 32 x 20: the top surface starts at row 4; rows 0-3 are clear except a vise at x 1-5 and ingots at x 26-31, so a creature (drawn smaller, behind) stands at x 8-24 and its lower rows hide behind the bench.
- `floor` 16 x 16 tiles both ways. `barrel` 12 x 16, `quench-trough` 24 x 12, `coal-heap` 16 x 10 stand on the floor (bottom row = base).
- New pieces (2026-11-14, from Misa's staging notes). Clickable, drawn bold (ink outline, lit edges, a glint): `door` 20 x 32 (plank leaf in a timber frame, two iron strap hinges, a ring handle, a stone step; the base row is the floor line), `door-mat` 20 x 4 (lies in front of the door), `plans-board` 24 x 24 (a drafting board with blue plans, white lines, pins and a pencil on trestle legs, a rolled plan on the bar), `finished-crate` 20 x 16 (an open crate with a steel helmet, a charm on a gold ring with a glint, and a striped scarf end over the side). They replace the plank, the 16 x 16 table and the stick crate of `valley/forge-props.ts`.
- Edge dressing (not clickable; quieter: soft soot outline `z` instead of ink, mid tones, no lit edges, no glint): `barrel-stack` 24 x 24 (three barrels), `sacks` 18 x 13, `gear-rack` 22 x 26 (a free standing rack with hats on pegs and scarves on a bar), `rug` 48 x 16 (a fixed worn oval; lies flat on the floor, drawn before everything that stands on it), `woodpile` 28 x 19, `cat` 12 x 8 (an ordinary cat asleep, by the furnace; warm on its fire side), `bucket` 10 x 10, `window-2` 12 x 31 (a narrow window for the side wall: lintel rows 0-3, opening 4-25, sill 26-30; repeat it with a 4 px gap), `lantern-hanging` 24 x 40 (a chain from the beam, row 0 touches the beam bottom, the lantern at x 8-15; the warm light on the wall is dithered, so the stones show through, at night in three warm steps; by day the light colours are the plain wall and only the glass stays lit).
- The room, 128 x 176 for a phone (a tall phone shows about 130 x 281 world px at 3x, so the room is meant to be scaled to the screen width and, if there is spare height, shown from the top with the front zone cut off or the room centred): the back wall stays 56 tall (y 0-55), the floor tiles run from y 56 to 175 (7.5 tiles; tiles start at y 56), then bands. Wall band y 0-55; furnace and bench band y 56-85 (the furnace light, the cat, the coal, the door and its mat); work band y 86-135 (anvils, chest, plans, finished crate, trough); front zone y 136-175 (rug, woodpile, sacks, barrels, gear rack, bucket). On desktop the room widens by tiling `back-wall` and `floor` sideways and by adding wall pieces on the new wall (window-2, tool-rack, hanging-tools, a second lantern, shelves) and floor dressing at the new left and right edges (barrel-stack, sacks, woodpile, gear-rack); the clickable pieces and the furnace stay centred on x 64 (the middle of the phone room), so nothing clickable moves apart.
- The 128 x 176 preview is taller than the studio allows (64), so it is three sprites that stack: `preview-top` (rows 0-63), `preview-middle` (rows 64-127), `preview-bottom` (rows 128-175). The room has more than 16 colours (borrowed creature colours). - Each light has its own colour: fire orange (bonfires), window yellow (school), violet lamp (visitor), a weak ember (visitor away), teal shard glow (market).
- Day ground given its own character (Misa, 2026-10-31).
- Day ground pushed further and the market crystal seated (Misa, 2026-10-31).
- House, Forge and Cave added in the same style for the valley's night (valley session request, 2026-11-03).
- The content needs the places to exist (V-BON, school, visitor, V-FORGE-11) before this art is used; the signs carry no text, only marks (a moon and a calendar on the visitor away board).

Each building can absolutely change building material as it upgrades in levels, and I'm thinking we might even want to tweak the earlier levels to be less elaborate... If you change materials, there needs to be a common motif between buildings of the same level... Think of how Clash of Clans brings a new look with each new town hall level."

- Level 1 Humble: a small fire in a loose ring of fieldstones on packed earth, one log to sit on (rope lashing, pale cut ends) and two sticks. Seat: (47, 52).

The firewood pile, and the crane and cauldron, are gone.
- Level 4 Valley: the stone pit on a paved floor lit by the fire, teal-and-cream cushions on the three seats, and a teal-and-cream banner on a short pole at each side with a brass cap. Seats as level 3. Misa 2026-11-11 (Redo): "This is really nice but let's drop the lamps." The brass lamps are gone; the banners stand on their own poles.
- Level 5 Crystal: a stone brazier with two gold bands and crystal shards set into it and crowning it (the crystal glows by day too), gold-edged stone benches with crystal inlays, crystal inlay in the paving, and a curved low sandstone wall behind the fire with gold coping and a crystal at each shoulder. Seats as level 3. Misa 2026-11-11 (Redo): "Drop the posts and move the gold and crystal motif more strongly into the brazier and benches. Add a curved supporting wall behind the fire." The crystal posts are gone.

## The Forge, level by level

![The Forge, level by level](valley-levels-forge.png)

- **Status:** draft
- **Requested:** 2026-11-09 (Misa): "Each building can absolutely change building material as it upgrades in levels ... Naturally a forge can't be made of wood, but it can have wooden elements on it ... Think of how Clash of Clans brings a new look with each new town hall level."
- **Source:** `apps/activity/src/sprites/concepts/valley-levels-forge.ts` (draw it with `pnpm art valley-levels-forge`)
- **Sheet of:** `5345a8584080`
- Five levels on one 56x60 canvas, all standing on row 51, centred; smaller levels leave the top and sides empty. Colours from valley-tiers, 16 or fewer per sprite.
- Night is the main palette with the ember glow lying on the ground in stepped rings in front of the fire; alts.day is the same pixels with the fire still lit and a soot-dark yard.
- Level 1 Humble: an open-air smithy: a fieldstone hearth mound with a small fire, a stump with a small anvil, a crooked rope-lashed log frame under a straw roof.
- Level 2 Settled: a small fieldstone forge in a sawn-timber frame under a red-brown shingle roof, a stone chimney, a bellows, a plank sign with a hammer.
- Level 3 Stone: a cut-stone smithy with a slate roof, black iron eave band and lintel, a tall stone chimney, a plank door with iron hinges and a big iron anvil.
- Level 4 Valley: the stone forge with a teal-and-cream awning over the fire, a teal pennant, brass lamps, a glass window and a quench trough.
- Level 5 Crystal: the master forge: a glowing crystal finial on the chimney, crystal inlays and pane, gold trim on eaves and lintel, gold lamps, sparks. The crystal glows by day too.
- 2026-11-11 (Misa), redo of levels 2 to 5: "Chimneys are floating in all of these." Each chimney now rises out of the roof: drawn first and carried down behind the roof, so the shingles or slates cut its foot, its outline closes on the roof line, and no gap is left. Level 1 has no chimney.

Bell box top-left (x, y): level 1 (53, 37) on the post arm; level 2 (52, 38) in the timber frame; levels 3, 4 and 5 (29, 18) in the tower opening. The same numbers are `SCHOOL_BELL_BOXES` in the set file.
- Level 1 Humble (log hut, thatch, one window, bell on a rope-lashed post beside it); 2 Settled (planks, shingles, two windows, plank sign, bell on a timber frame); 3 Stone (sandstone walls, terracotta roof, bell tower over the door, black iron bands); 4 Valley (cream trim, teal shutters, a teal-and-cream pennant on the tower, brass lamps by the door, glass windows); 5 Crystal (a crystal on the tower spire and an inlay on its face, gold eaves, a wider hall with four windows).
- Window light spills on the grass at night; by day the windows are plain glass (the lamps too). Crystal stays teal by day.

## The School's visiting teacher

![The School's visiting teacher](valley-school.png)

- **Status:** draft
- **Requested:** 2026-11-03 (via the valley session, Misa's round 22 decision): show the visiting teacher with no banner: the bell swings, a lectern at the door, a bench of students, a teacher prop.
- **Source:** `apps/activity/src/sprites/concepts/valley-school.ts` (draw it with `pnpm art valley-school`)
- **Sheet of:** `764ab7d8ac30`
- Lead's review (2026-11-03): the yard's window light is kept faint on purpose, because the School sprite throws its own spill and students on the bench cover most of it. Push it brighter if it should read on its own. Talent icons need no new art: the four combat v2 role glyphs already ship (Setter `mark`, Payoff `sparkle`, Guard `shield`, Support `ability`).
- Spec: valley/systems/school.md, "As decided (round 22)": no banner; the bell swings and a lectern appears at the door before the teacher comes, the teacher stands at the lectern Monday to Wednesday, students sit on a bench in front (empty seats show there is room to join), at dusk the windows light.
- Lectern: the camp's `lectern` (48x50) is as big as the School itself, so beside a 16x16 teacher it is too big for the yard; `school-lectern` (22x17) is a small stand for the yard. Its foot is (10, 15) in its own pixels; the game puts that point at yard (73, 14). The teacher stands left of it, feet (62, 14): the sprite's top-left is (54, -1). Draw order: yard, lectern, teacher, then the students.
- Yard: 80x24 (wider than the 64 asked: the bench takes the left 56 px and the right 24 px are the clear spot for the lectern and the teacher). Placed so the yard's x 31 and 32 are under the School door (yard top-left = School top-left + (-2, 38)), top row against the door steps; the two warm pools are under the School's two windows (yard x 21 and 42). Four seats on one long bench, 13 px apart. A creature is drawn with its sprite's bottom row (its feet, the last row, 15) on the seat row, so its top-left is (seat x - 8, 12 - 15): seat feet points (9, 12), (22, 12), (35, 12), (48, 12) in yard pixels (plank top rows 11 and 12; the front face below is clear). Nothing is drawn above row 10 over the bench, so the seats are unobstructed; an empty seat is just bare plank. Day: bare dirt, pebbles and grass tufts at the edge, no light.
- Bell: three 6x6 overlays for the School's cupola opening; top-left (27, 7) on the 60x50 School sprite. `school-bell` is the School's own pixels at rest (a test checks it against `valley-glow.ts`); `left` and `right` tilt the 2x2 bronze bell one pixel across and one row apart. Play rest, left, rest, right while the bell rings. The day alt uses the School's own day colours for the same keys.
- Teacher cap: a navy mortarboard (a flat diamond board with a lighter top face and an ink underside), a small cap under it, a gold button, a gold cord to the right corner and a gold tassel hanging beside the head. It is fixed colour (not item-tinted). How it plugs in: a new hat class `mortarboard` in `worn-sprites.ts` would hold the board and cap as a `HalfShape` (rows 0 to 5, left half, mirrored; the top face of the board in rows 1 and 2 is drawn a little off-centre and the cord crosses row 2, so a mirrored version makes those two rows symmetric and leaves the cord to the patch) and `wearing()` would paint the tassel patch (the three cord and tassel columns, x 13 to 14, rows 2 to 7 of the cap) on the right as a second small shape; a hat that is taller than the usual rule puts its top row two rows above the head top (the usual rule puts its bottom row one under the head top), so ears stay visible beside the board. Face rows 8 to 10 are never painted; the tassel is the only part that can reach row 8 and 9, at x 13 to 14, beside the cheek.
- The variants of `teacher-cap` show it on three shipped creatures: Splashet (round), Sproutle (leaf ears) and Zipmouse (small, ears and a tail on the right, so its tassel hangs on the left). They are composed in code from the shipped sprites, not drawn by hand.
